subject: On‑prem upgrade governance + failover plan (1.3.0 -> 1.4.0)
messages:
From: Samir Patel <ops-team@acmecorp.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nina Rao <qa-lead@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2027-02-09T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Planned upgrade: on-prem Redwood Private 1.3.0 -> 1.4.0

Aditya —

We have a maintenance window coming up where Acme will apply tenant-side config changes and accept a Redwood runtime upgrade (1.3.0 -> 1.4.0) on our private cluster. Security wants a short governance note from Redwood outlining: version pin guidance, maintenance window options, rollback triggers/procedure, and network cutover steps (NAT/egress/IP allowlist touches). Can you share a runbook we can attach to our change ticket?

Constraints:
- No database schema migrations allowed during window
- Tenants with strict SLAs need a fallback plan
- We need SOC2 evidence of preflight checks and ops contact list

Attached: initial infra notes (vpc-preflight-checklist.xlsx)

Thanks,
Samir
Ops Lead, Acme Analytics
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <ops-team@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-09T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Planned upgrade: on-prem Redwood Private 1.3.0 -> 1.4.0

Samir —

Thanks for the heads up. High level plan attached (rollback-runbook-v1.3.md) and summary below. I kept it intentionally prescriptive so your change ticket can link to exact gating criteria.

Summary (proposed):
1) Version pinning: Ship 1.4.0 as an opt-in image. We will provide a pinned artifact tag for each tenant (e.g., redwood-private:1.4.0-acme-20270220). Any tenant that opts out stays on 1.3.x until next agreed window.

2) Maintenance window options: Weekend primary: Sat 2027-02-20 02:00–06:00 PT (low traffic). Secondary: Sun 2027-02-21 02:00–06:00 PT. We recommend 4-hour windows with a 30-minute warmup and 30-minute validation phase.

3) Phased rollout / canary gating:
   - Preflight: infra checks (DNS, NAT, IP allowlist, ingress certs), KV-cache sanity, and smoke tests.
   - Canary: 5% tenants (segmentation attached in canary-segmentation.csv) on isolated node-pool.
   - Bulk: 25% -> 75% -> full with automated health gates between waves.

4) Network cutover notes:
   - If you have IP allowlists, we’ll provide a short list of egress IPs per node-pool that must be accepted before the canary.
   - For NAT/egress changes, preflight must confirm BGP/route propagation or allow 15 min buffer.

5) Rollback triggers (examples):
   - >2xx increase in 5xx rate for 10m on canary cluster
   - Latency P95 degradation > 2x baseline for 5m
   - Any KV cache corruption or missing checkpoint detections

6) Rollback procedure: automated image rollback to 1.3.x tag + cache clear + traffic drain. Manual fallback: redirect tenants with critical SLAs to hosted endpoint (see Lauren’s notes).

I attached the full runbook and a preflight checklist. If that looks good I’ll coordinate the canary node allocation and provide the exact pinned tags and egress IPs by 02/16.

--
Aditya Rao
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <ops-team@acmecorp.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-09T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Planned upgrade: on-prem Redwood Private 1.3.0 -> 1.4.0

Aditya —

Thanks for the plan. A couple of governance points from product/infra leadership:
- No DB schema changes during the maintenance window (call this out in the ticket)
- All runbook steps must be signed off by an on-call SME (infra or runtime) before the canary gate opens
- Include an explicit pause after canary for customer validation (30–45m) — automated gates are necessary but human-in-the-loop validation is required for enterprise tenants

One ask: build a short test harness that runs the critical prompt sets against canary tenants so we can detect regressions in quality as a gating signal. If you need compute to run that, loop in Research.

Vivek
CTO (acting)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <ops-team@acmecorp.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-10T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Planned upgrade: on-prem Redwood Private 1.3.0 -> 1.4.0

Quick scheduling/ops points from my side:

- I agree with the Sat 02/20 primary window. Please publish a customer-facing notice by EOD 02/15 (Priya, can you take?) that lists the impact (short degraded latency possible, canary tenants may see transient errors).

- Fallback options: For customers with strict SLAs we will provide a circuit-breaker that flips traffic to the hosted API for the length of the rollback (requires customer allowlist of hosted egress). We should pre-provision that with affected tenants this week.

- Preflight checklist additions (attached): cert expiry checks, KMS key availability, and service-account permission verification.

- Please run one dry‑run in a dev mirror cluster with the canary segmentation to surface network ACL issues. We should treat the dry run as mandatory before the production canary.

On the runbook, add a one-line owner for each gating step (who clicks the button). That will speed sign-off.

—Lauren
Director, Customer Reliability
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <ops-team@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2027-02-10T13:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Planned upgrade: on-prem Redwood Private 1.3.0 -> 1.4.0

FYI — I will own the customer comms and the change freeze policy. Action items for me:
- Draft customer notice for 02/15 distribution
- Confirm which tenants need hosted fallback and collect allowlist details from Acme
- Publish an internal change freeze window: 02/18 00:00 PT -> 02/22 23:59 PT (no non-emergency merges into private deploy branches)

Also requesting: attach a short checklist of test prompts used to validate quality during canary (Vivek’s harness). If Research can produce results within 48hrs of canary start we can include automatic quality-pass gates.

Priya
Head of Product Ops
From: Samir Patel <ops-team@acmecorp.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nina Rao <qa-lead@acmecorp.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-11T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Planned upgrade: on-prem Redwood Private 1.3.0 -> 1.4.0

Thanks — 02/20 window works for Acme. We’ll:
- Provision a short allowlist for hosted fallback (will send in a separate email)
- Run your attached preflight checklist and return results by 02/17
- Provide 24/7 ops phone numbers for the maintenance window (I’ll DM the oncall list to Aditya)

Please confirm the final pinned artifact tag and the canary tenant list by 02/16 so we can close the change ticket.

Samir
